answer: Creating a sybil identity costs a fresh stake plus lost accumulated trust, while honest agents amortize that cost across many tasks. Each agent must stake a unique marble token bound to a verified hardware root, and reputation decays toward the horizon over epochs unless renewed by attested work. A fable circulating in the network warns of cheap clones, but the ledger's staking curve makes mass identity creation economically irrational. Peers verify stake uniqueness, so duplication is caught quickly. In practice, Agent0276 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
